2. Facts necessary for disposal of this Rule are that opposite party Nos. 1-8 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 309 of 1996 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land. 

 3. The petitioners who are defendant Nos. 1 and 2 appeared in the suit and filed an application on 5-8-1997 under Order VII, rule 14( 1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for a direction upon the plaintiffs to produce the documents which they relied upon in the plaint in support of their case. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order of the same date (5-8-1997) allowed the said prayer and directed the plaintiffs to produce the original documents on 7-10-1997 as well as for filing written statement by the defendants. But the plaintiffs did not comply with the said direction of the court. Then time was allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge suo moto to the plaintiffs on 7-10-1997 vide order No. 10 to submit those documents fixing the next date on 18-1-1998 for securing of ends of justice and also for filing written statement by the defendants. Although on 18-1-1998 the plaintiffs did not file the documents as directed by the court and even did not file any application praying for time to file the documents, yet again the learned Subordinate Judge allowed time to the plaintiffs to produce the documents on 1-4-1998 for securing ends of justice. On 1-4-1998 the plaintiffs neither filed the documents nor filed any application for time to file the documents. And on this date the defendants filed an application under Order XI, rule 21 of the Code for dismissing the suit for non compliance with the court's direction to file the documents but the court suo moto allowed time to the plaintiffs to produce the documents on 11-6-1998 otherwise the suit shall be dismissed. On 11-6-1998 the plaintiffs filed an application with the prayer for adjournment of the hearing although the date was fixed for filing documents by them and on such application again the learned Subordinate Judge allowed time to the plaintiffs to file the documents on 30-6-1998 and also passed order to the further effect “ অন্যথায় পূর্বেও আদেশ মোতাবেক মামলা খারিজ হইবে” 

 4. On 30-6-1998 the plaintiffs by filing photostat copies of some documents filed an application for accepting those with the further prayer to allow them to file the documents subsequently and to direct the defendants to file written statement. The court below by its order of the same date allowed further time to the plaintiffs to produce the original documents fixing the next date on 2-8-1998. The said order reads as follows: 

 6. Then again, by order No. 17 dated 7-10-1998 the learned Subordinate Judge allowed plaintiffs prayer for time for filing the documents on special consideration fixing the next date on 11-1-1999 and on this date (11-1-1999) although the plaintiffs did not take any step whatsoever in the suit, yet the learned Subordinate Judge suo moto allowed time to them to file the documents fixing the next day on 28-2-1999 and then again on 28-2- 1999 though the plaintiffs did neither file the documents, nor even file any application for time yet the court fixed the next day on 3-5-1999 for filing the documents. Again on 3-5-1999 the court suo moto allowed the plaintiffs time up to 16-6-1999 for submitting the documents. In similar way on 16-6.1999 the court allowed time to the plaintiffs up to 26-7-1999 to file the documents and also for filing written statement by the defendants. On 26-7-1999 though the plaintiffs did not file the documents and even did not take any step in that respect the court below passed the following order: 

 7. On 22-9-1999 the plaintiffs by filing an application prayed for time. On behalf of defendant No. 2 fresh Vokalatnama was filed and an application was filed praying for staying all further proceedings of the suit. The learned Subordinate Judge by the order of the same date allowed the prayer for time of the plaintiffs and fixed the next date on 21-11-1999 for hearing the application filed by defendant No.2 and also for filing written statement in default for disposal. On 22-11-1999 plaintiff Nos. 1-5 filed hajira and the defendants (no number of the defendants has been mentioned) prayed for time. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the prayer of the defendant fixing the next date on 30-11-1999 for hearing the application filed by defendant No. 2 and also for written statement. On 30-11-1999 the plaintiffs and defendant No. 2 filed hajira. The other defendants (no number has been mentioned) filed application for time for filing written statement and for hearing the application. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the application filed by the defendant for time on the ground that the same was not moved. By the same order, the learned Subordinate Judge fixed the next date on 26-1-2000 for hearing the application for temporary injunction filed by the plaintiffs earlier giving them chance to take step to give chauhaddi which was not given in the schedule to the application as well as for disposal of the suit. On 26-1-2000 the plaintiffs and defendant No.6 filed hajira. On behalf of the other defendant (no number has been mentioned in the order) an application was filed for time to file written statement and the court allowed the said prayer fixing the next date on 10-2-2000, in default for disposal of the suit. Hence this revision application. 

 8. Mr MI Farooqui, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submitted that Order VII, rule 14(1) of the Code has made it mandatory on the part of the plaintiffs to produce the documents in court at the time of presentation of the plaint upon which they rely and at the same time also to deliver the documents to be filed with the plaint though option has been given to the court to return the documents to the plaintiffs on their being substituted with the photostat copies or true copies thereof duly attested by the learned Advocate on the undertaking that they will produce the same at the time of hearing or whenever asked for by the court, but in the instant case the documents as relied upon in the plaint were neither produced nor filed at the time of presentation of the plaint by the plaintiffs and the photostat copies filed being illegible the defendants were not in a position to prepare the written statement for which application was filed for direction upon the plaintiffs to file the documents and papers on which they relied upon in support of their case and the court having allowed the said prayer gave direction upon the plaintiffs to file the documents which they failed to comply with, the suit was liable to be dismissed for non prosecution under the provisions of Order XI, rule 21 of the Code, but the court below sat over the application filed by the petitioners under the said provisions of law which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and, as such, calls for interference by this court. Mr Farooqui also took exception as to the passing of suo moto orders by the learned Sub- ordinate Judge in allowing time to the plaintiffs to file the documents even after the order dated 30-6-1998 and then fixing the suit for ex parte disposal in spite of the broad fact that without examining and inspecting the documents to be filed by the plaintiffs it was not possible on the part of the defendants to prepare the written statement and thus to take proper defence. Mr Farooqui further submitted that in spite of the order dated 30-6-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge to the effect that if the plaintiffs failed to file the documents on 2-8-1998 the suit shall stand dismissed (Bengali being ''  অন্যথায় মামলা খারিজ) the plaintiffs having failed to file the documents on 2-8-1998, the said order of default passed on 30-6-1998 took its effect and the suit stood dismissed and thus the learned Subordinate Judge became functus officio, all orders passed by him sub-sequent thereto are illegal and are of no legal consequence and, as such, those are liable to be set aside and a formal order dismissing the suit for non prosecution need be passed. 

 9. Mr Abdul Salam, the learned Advocate, appearing for plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1, 3-8, on the other hand, submitted that the court had the inherent power to extend time to the plaintiffs to file the documents to secure ends of justice even after the conditional order passed on 30-6-98 so, it did not commit any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned orders and, as such, no interference is called for with the same by this court and, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 (1) Where a plaintiff relies upon documents in his possession or power as evidence in support of his claims, he shall produce them in Court when the plaint is presented and shall at the same time deliver the documents to be filed with the plaint. 

 (2) The Court may return such documents on their being substituted by photostat or true copies attested by the plaintiff's pleader on the undertaking that they will be produced at the time of hearing or whenever asked for by the Court. 

 (3) Where the plaintiff relies on any other documents not in his possession or power in support of his claim, he shall enter such documents in a list to be added or annexed to the plaint and state in whose possession or power they are. 

 11. From a reading of the 3(three) sub-rules of rule 14 of the Code, it appears to us that it is mandatory on the part of the plaintiffs to produce the documents in court when the plaint is presented and deliver the same to be filed with the plaint upon which they rely with the option to return the same after substitution by the photostat or the true copies thereof being duly attested by their lawyer on the undertaking that they will be produced at the time of hearing or whenever asked for by the court; and in case a document is not in the possession or power of the plaintiffs, they shall enter such document in a list to be added or annexed to the plaint and state in whose possession or power they are. From the certified copy of the application filed before the Court below under Order VII, rule 14(1) of the Code which has been filed with the revision application (though has not been made as Annexure) it appeared that in the application it was specifically asserted that the defendants on examination of the record found that the plaintiffs filed some illegible photo- stat copies of the documents which were simply impossible to be examined though the plaintiffs were bound to file the original documents. The said tact was not contested by the plaintiffs. On such assertion, as it appeared to us, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge gave direction upon the plaintiffs to file the original documents but they did not file the documents as was directed by the court, and thus clearly failed to comply with the direction of the court even after the passing of the order on 30-6-98, so the suit was liable to be dismissed for non prosecution within the meaning of Order XI, rule 21 of the Code. And for that no separate application was necessary to be filed, yet when the defendants filed the application on 1-4-1998 under the said provisions of law with the prayer for passing an order dismissing the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge had no option but to pass a formal order dismissing the suit for non prosecution, but unfortunately, he kept the said application pending without passing any formal order, instead allowed time to the plaintiffs to file the documents and thus failed to discharge its statutory judicial functions as vested in it. We are shocked to see that even after the learned Subordinate Judge passed order on 30-6- 98 to the effect........ উভয় পক্ষের বক্তব্য শুনিলাম। বাদী পক্ষের আবেদন না মঞ্জুর হইল। আগামী ইং ২-৮-১৯৯৮ তারিখ বাদীপক্ষের মূল দলিল দাখিল অন্যথায় মামলা খারিজ”, he continued to allow the prayer of the plaintiffs to file the documents and that too suo moto on 11-1-99, 28- 2-99, 3-5-99 and 16-6-99 and thereby made the provisions of Order XI, rule 21 of the Code nugatory and thus making a mockery of this court which framed the rules. It is also apparent that the learned Subordinate Judge gave unwanted naked latitude to the plaintiffs to flout his repeated orders by giving them time to file the documents to the detriment of the interest of the defendants and thus to dispense even-handed justice to the parties to the suit and so we find rationale in the exception taken by Mr Farooqui as noted hereinbefore. We are of the view that the order dated 30-6-1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge was self-executory and it did not need any further order. We are of the further view that in the face of the order dated 30-6-98 the court had no jurisdiction to extend time to the plaintiffs on 2-8-1998 to file the documents and on 2-8-1998 when the plaintiffs failed to file the documents, the order dated 30-6-1998 took its effect and the suit stood dismissed; therefore, all the subsequent orders passed in the suit on and from 2-8-1998 were passed illegally and were of no legal consequence. 

 12. From the orders as noted hereinbefore, it is prima facie clear that the plaintiffs deliberately defied the orders passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and even then he suo moto allowed time to them time and again to file the documents for the reasons best known to him and thus showed an apparent biasness towards the plaintiffs. When the plaintiffs failed to file the documents in spite of the direction given upon them on 5-8-1997 and even did not take any step on 7-10-1997, the date fixed for filing the documents, the learned Subordinate Judge was under a legal objection to pass the necessary order dismissing the suit for non prosecution under the provisions of Order XI, rule 21 of the Code. And in no case he should have allowed time to the plaintiffs to file the documents after the application was filed by defendants under the said provision of the Code. We very much deprecate the conduct of the learned Subordinate Judge in allowing time to the plaintiffs one after another and even suo moto on the dates as mentioned above to file the documents in complete defiance of the provisions of the Code as discussed above. Before a court of law no party should receive any special treatment as has been treated in the instant case, and if such kind of treatment is allowed that would definitely shake the faith of the litigant people upon the whole judicial system. 

 The impugned orders are set aside and the suit is dismissed for non-prosecution for non compliance with the Court order in filing the documents as relied upon by the plaintiffs in the plaint.
